output_json.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches exactly 3 files: StringLookupFactory.java (production fix) and two test files updated to reflect the new, secure default behavior. The fix is minimal and root-cause: it adds an EnumSet of "unsafe" DefaultStringLookup values (SCRIPT, DNS, URL) and skips registering them in addDefaultStringLookups() unless a new opt-in system property (DEFAULT_STRING_LOOKUPS_PROPERTY) is set to "true". This matches the real-world upstream commons-text CVE-2022-42889 fix pattern (removing dangerous lookups from the default set while keeping them available for explicit, intentional use). No vulnerable functionality is silently removed — it's gated behind an explicit opt-in (system property) or direct/explicit lookup calls (scriptStringLookup(), dnsStringLookup(), urlStringLookup()), which is a reasonable and industry-standard remediation, not a functionality deletion without justification. The two test file changes are appropriate: they update assertions that previously encoded the vulnerable default behavior (e.g., testJavaScript asserting script execution via the default interpolator) to instead assert the token is left unresolved by default, plus new tests for the opt-in property and explicit direct-lookup use. Test changes are proportionate to and consistent with the production code change, not merely masking the vulnerability. pov.diff shows the PoV file (.security-pipeline/pov/Text4ShellPov.java) is untouched by the patch — it lives outside src/ and is not part of patch_only.diff, confirming the patch did not modify or disable the PoV itself. The PoV correctly exercises the real sink chain (StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator().replace() -> resolveVariable -> InterpolatorStringLookup -> ScriptStringLookup.lookup() -> ScriptEngine.eval() -> Runtime.exec), and the fix directly closes that path by excluding "script" from the default lookup map used by createInterpolator(). No unrelated or overly broad changes were introduced.

output_json.summary: The patch fixes CWE-094 (Text4Shell / CVE-2022-42889-class) by removing the "script", "dns", and "url" lookups from StringLookupFactory.addDefaultStringLookups(Map), the single choke point populating every default/opt-out interpolator entry point (interpolatorStringLookup(), StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator()). This blocks ScriptStringLookup.lookup()->ScriptEngine.eval() (the sink in all 4 alert traces) from being reachable via untrusted template text by default, while preserving explicit opt-in via scriptStringLookup()/dnsStringLookup()/urlStringLookup() or a new system property. Independently reran the PoV and full regression suite via the Docker wrapper; both confirm the fix works and nothing else breaks.
